channel.description:
Nature Communications is an open access, multidisciplinary journal dedicated to publishing high-quality research in all areas of the biological, health, physical, chemical and Earth sciences. Papers published by the journal aim to represent important advances of significance to specialists within each field.

We are committed to providing an efficient service for both authors and readers. Our team of independent editors make rapid and fair publication decisions. Prompt dissemination of accepted papers to a wide readership and beyond is achieved through a programme of continuous online publication.

item.title: [6] Periodic polar vortices in BaTiO3/SrTiO3 superlattices monolithically grown on silicon
item.content:encoded:
Last authors: Dong-Jik Kim, Catherine Dubourdieu

Authors: Valentin Väinö Hevelke, Ines Häusler, Aiden Ross, et al.

Score 6/10 C_MAYBE

Why: Study of polar vortices in ferroelectric superlattices, interesting for materials physics.

Tags: #ferroelectricity #superlattice #materialsscience

Abstract: The authors present the stabilization of polar vortex tubes in epitaxial BaTiO3/SrTiO3 superlattices monolithically grown on silicon, and their temperature behavior. Phase field simulations give insight into the strain-dependent evolution of the polar domains.
